touches.text: It outputs only its findings. It certifies nothing, records no crossing, and posts nothing; the gate consumes its findings.

A rule not yet enforced is made into a ticket now. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#89: "i said no ious because you were making a lot of them. ious have to be made into tickets. if we have them floating around, then they need to be made tickets NOW." So ticket f5dbfddea8c6 makes the rewrites it proposed at the 24 remaining sites (CLAUDE.md, MAP.md, the press office, PROOF.md). Where a site names a rule whose physics is not built, it names that rule's real ticket id, cast now if none exists; the word "ticket" with no id behind it does not count. CC's reading of his answer, on a mechanism CC made.

What a gate asks is "does this meet the intentions", never who did it. Every intention carries a why, and so does every test case whose purpose is not plain. A change that makes a ticket or a test case meet the intentions better is good, and downstream supports it when the whys show it isn't a fast one. Measuring who did what serves none of that.

The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Either way the system improves. WHY: a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or its implementation, never a conversation about procedure. The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure, and it is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome. Nothing passes a ticket over a red.

Every sieve carries its own why, and the why names where it came from. Akien designed the inspector tools; CC built each specific sieve from what it read him to mean. So the adjudication in 17.11.6 is against the sieve's own why, done by CC, and never a question to him. Akien 2026-11-13: "I designed the tools, but not the specific sieves. you built those to handle what you thought i meant for each inspector. ... i don't know why each sieve is there. we are supposed to add a why to each sieve so we can help adjudicate it. and this is also why the sieves are not perfect. Nothing in this system ever will be perfect. the whole thing will constantly be under improvement." Measured that day: build_inspector registers 43 sieves, and the 36 sieves/*.json records carry name, band and dials but no why. The whys live only in docstrings.

Deleting code is about running code, not about the record of what happened. A retired path that something still CALLS is the defect; a retired path named by a record of what passed through (history, state, validations, verdicts, a measured fixture) is not. Requirements that police history are de-emphasized, because the aim is less history noise in front of Claude, not hidden history (Law 5). Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#99 (ticket c8e421aac06e's measured fixture names skills/ruled/intention+why.json and the retirement tooth read it as a caller): "we are trying to remove as much of the history as we can. not hiding it, but reducing the noise you're exposed to. time to de-emphasize requirements like that."
